scroll verb

on a screen

modern

Traupman 262, 375

dēvolvō, dēvolvere, dēvolvī, dēvolūtum

verb, third conjugation

roll down: scroll down

Traupman’s verb for scrolling down; classically to roll something down (Caes. BC 2.11.1, of rocks). The Roman book was itself a scroll, read by unrolling it, ēvolvere volūmen (Cic. Att. 9.10.4), so the figure is an old one. To scroll back up, revolvere, to roll back.

See also swipe, screen, mouse.

SourcesLewis & Short: devolvo · Lewis & Short: evolvo · Lewis & Short: revolvo · Lewis & Short: volumen

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 262, 375.
